 THIS MISCELLANEOUS FIRST APPEAL FILED UNDER SECTION 173(1) OF THE MOTOR VEHICLES ACT, THIS HON'BLE COURT BE PLEASED TO MODIFY THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED 14.12.2015 PASSED BY THE MACT-II, AT BALLARI IN MVC.
NO.1155/2014 BY ENHANCING THE COMPENSATION TO THE APPELLANT AND PASS SUCH OTHER ORDER OR ORDERS AS THIS HON'BLE COURT DEEMS FIT IN THE CIRCUMSTANCES IN THE INTEREST OF JUSTICE AND EQUITY.

THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS DAY,
VIJAYKUMAR A. PATIL, J., DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT

This appeal is filed by the parents of the deceased Mahammed Yunus being aggrieved by the judgment and award dated 14.12.2015 passed by the Motor Accidents Claim Tribunal-II, Ballari in M.V.C. No.1154/2014 seeking for enhancement of the compensation.

B. Vali Sab S/O Usman Sab vs G. Srinivasa S/O G. Shivarangaiah on 20 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/107969697/
2 2.

Brief facts of the case giving rise to filing of this appeal are that on 08.10.2014 at 10.30 p.m.,
Mahammed NC: 2023:KHC-D:7557-DB Yunus, the son of the claimants was proceeding on his motorcycle on Kampli-Kurugodu road.
When he reached near Srinivasa Camp, Ballari Taluk, driver of the tractor bearing No.KA-34/T-4232 came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against Mahammed Yunus.
Due to the said impact, Mahammed Yunus sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the injuries on the spot.
It is averred that prior to the accident, the deceased was aged about 20 years, was working as welder and earning Rs.18,000/- p.m.
It is further averred that the deceased was contributing his earnings towards family.
It is averred that due to the rash and negligent driving by the driver of tractor, the accident has occurred.
It is further averred that respondent Nos.2 and 3 being the owner and insurer of offending vehicle, are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.

3. Though all the respondents entered appearance, respondent No.3-insurance company filed written statement denying the averments of the claim petition by NC: 2023:KHC-D:7557-DB stating that the accident in question has not taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the tractor.

It is averred that the claimants have not produced any documents to establish that the respondent No.1 was the driver of the offending tractor at the time of accident, however, it was admitted that the said vehicle was insured with them.
It is further averred that the accident took place due to rash and negligent riding of the motorcycle by the deceased himself.
The insurance company denied the earning of the deceased.

It is also averred that the respondent No.1 was not having valid and effective driving licence and respondent No.2 being the owner had entrusted the vehicle to the respondent No.1, hence, respondent No.2 has violated the policy conditions and prayed for dismissal of the claim petition.
4. The Tribunal framed the issues and recorded evidence of the parties.
The 1st appellant/father of the deceased examined himself as PW-1 and got marked Exs.P-1 to P-13.
The respondent-insurance company did NC: 2023:KHC-D:7557-DB not examine any witness, however, got marked policy at Ex.R-1.

The Tribunal on appreciation of material evidence available on record, partly allowed the claim petition and awarded compensation of Rs.5,10,000/- with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till realisation on the following heads:
1. Towards loss of dependency Rs.4,20,000/-
2. Towards love and affection Rs.30,000/-
3. Towards funeral expenses Rs.30,000/-
4.

Towards loss of expectancy Rs.30,000/-
 Total Rs.5,10,000/-

3 appearing for Sri Y. Lakshmikant Reddy for appellant- claimants submits that the Tribunal has committed an error in assessing the income of the deceased at Rs.5,000/-p.m. as the deceased was working as Welder and earning Rs.18,000/- p.m.

sentences.text: It is submitted that the Tribunal has committed an error in applying 14 multiplier to the case on hand taking the age of the mother.
The deceased was aged about 20 years as on the date of accident.
Hence, the appropriate multiplier would be 18.
It is further submitted that the Tribunal has committed an error in not granting any compensation under the head of loss of future prospects.

It is further submitted that the Tribunal has committed grave error in not granting compensation under the head of loss of consortium as per the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Magma General Insurance Company Limited Vs Nanu Ram1.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is also submitted that the Tribunal has awarded meager compensation on other heads and she sought to enhance the same.

6. Per contra, learned counsel Sri S.S. Koliwad for respondent-insurance company supports the impugned judgment and award and submits that the appellants have failed to produce any evidence before the Tribunal with regard to income of the deceased.
Hence, the tribunal has notionally assessed the income of the deceased at Rs.5,000/- p.m.

It is submitted that the tribunal on appreciation of evidence on record, has awarded just and (2018) SCC 130 NC:
2023:KHC-D:7557-DB proper compensation on other heads, the same does not call for any modification in the present appeal and he seeks to dismiss the appeal.
7. We have heard the learned counsel for the appellant/claimants, learned counsel for the respondent, perused the memorandum of appeal and the Tribunal records.

8. The points that arise for consideration in this appeal are that:
(i) Whether the Tribunal is justified in assessing the income of the deceased at Rs.5,000/- p.m.?
(ii) Whether the appellant/claimants are entitled for enhancement of compensation?
9.

The aforementioned point No.1 is answered in the negative and point No.2 in affirmative for the following reasons:
10.
There is no dispute with regard to the accident and death of Mahammed Yunus in the said accident.
The NC: 2023:KHC-D:7557-DB Tribunal in the absence of any cogent and acceptable evidence has assessed the income of the deceased at Rs.5,000/- p.m.
In our considered view, the notional income assessed by the Tribunal is on the lower side.

This Court and Lok-adalaths while settling the disputes under the provisions of Motor Vehicles Act, base their reliance on the notional income chart prepared by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
As per the chart, the notional income for the accidents taken place in the year 2014 is to be assessed at Rs.7,500/- p.m.

In our considered view, in the absence of any cogent and acceptable evidence on record, basing our B. Vali Sab S/O Usman Sab vs G. Srinivasa S/O G. Shivarangaiah on 20 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/107969697/

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
4 reliance on the chart prepared by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, we assess the notional income of the deceased at Rs.7,500/- p.m.
11.
The Tribunal has committed error in not awarding the compensation under the head of future prospects.

Keeping in mind the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi and NC: 2023:KHC-D:7557-DB others2, we deem it appropriate that the appellant- claimants are entitled for addition of 40% to the assessed income towards loss of future prospects as the decease is aged 20 years.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi and NC: 2023:KHC-D:7557-DB others2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Tribunal has committed an error while awarding the compensation by applying 14 multiplier taking the age of the mother.
It is settled legal position that while applying multiplying, age of the deceased is to be taken and not the age of the parents or dependents.

As per the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court Sarla Verma and others Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation Limited and another3, the appropriate multiplier would be '18' as the deceased was aged about 20 years as on the date of accident.

entities.text: Sarla Verma and others Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation Limited and another3
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Tribunal has rightly deducted 50% of the assessed income towards personal and living expenses as the deceased was bachelor.
12. The Tribunal has committed an error in not awarding any compensation for loss of consortium.

As per the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the (2017) 16 SCC 680 2009 ACJ 1298 - 10 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:7557-DB case of Magma General Insurance Company Limited referred to supra,
both the appellants are entitled for Rs.40,000/- each towards loss of consortium.

The appellants are entitled for Rs.15,000/- towards transportation of dead body and funeral expenses and Rs.15,000/-
towards loss of estate.

13. Thus, the claimants are entitled for the compensation towards loss of dependency as under:
Rs.7,500 + 40%= Rs.10,500/-
Rs.10,500 - 5,250 (50% of Rs.10,500/-) = Rs.5,250/-
Rs.5,250 x 12 x 18 = Rs.11,34,000/-
14.

Thus, the claimants would be entitled for modified compensation on the following heads:
 Sl. Particulars Amount  No.
 1. Loss of dependency Rs.11,34,000/-

2 . Transportation of dead body Rs.15,000/-
 and funeral expenses  3. Loss of Estate Rs.15,000/-
 4. Loss of consortium Rs.80,000/-
 Total Rs.12,44,000/-
 Compensation awarded by the Rs.5,10,000/-

5  Enhanced compensation Rs.7,34,000/-

For the aforementioned reasons, we pass the following:
ORDER i) The appeal is allowed in part.
ii) The judgment and award dated 14.12.2015 passed by the Motor Accidents Claim Tribunal- II, Ballari in M.V.C. No.1154/2014 is modified and the appellant/claimants are entitled for enhanced compensation of Rs.7,34,000/- at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till realisation.
